flawed_step: 0006: The claim that every component of G=(V,M∪M′) is either an isolated vertex or a cycle is false. A common edge of M and M′ forms a two-vertex, one-edge component.
counterexample: Let T have V={1,2} and E={{1,2}}, and take M=M′={{1,2}}. Both are perfect matchings. Then G=(V,M∪M′) has one component: the edge joining 1 and 2. This component is neither an isolated vertex nor a cycle, contradicting step 0006.
assessment_summary: The proof’s main idea is repairable, but the stated component classification is incorrect. The correct classification is: every component of M∪M′ is either a single edge common to both matchings or an alternating even cycle. Since a tree has no cycles, only common-edge components occur, yielding M=M′.
